chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, from Ibrahim ibn Ishaq, from Ali ibn Muhammad, from al-Hasan ibn Dawud al-Raqqi, who said:

We were sitting with Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) when a man passed by with a slaughtered 'khattaf' (a type of bird) in his hand. Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) jumped at him and took it from his hand, then rolled it on the ground. He then said: 'Did your scholar command you to do this, or your jurist?' Indeed, my father informed me from my grandfather that the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) forbade the killing of six: the bee, the ant, the frog, the locust, the hoopoe, and the khattaf.

key_terms.أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (peace be upon him).
key_terms.خُطَّاف: A type of bird, often identified as a swift or swallow, mentioned in this hadith as one of the creatures whose killing is forbidden.

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on killing the khattaf bird in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Istibsar*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) physically demonstrates the ruling on the *khattaf* bird by taking a slaughtered specimen and rolling it on the ground, thereby questioning whether the people followed the command of the scholars or the jurists. He links this specific practice to a broader Prophetic tradition forbidding the killing of six creatures, including the bee, ant, frog, hoopoe, and *khattaf*, highlighting the continuity of divine law through the Ahl al-Bayt. This incident underscores the authority of the Imams in clarifying and enacting the Sunnah, serving as a practical lesson in distinguishing authentic religious directives from popular or scholarly assumptions.
